Respiratory: Alveolar‑capillary membrane, surfactant production by type II pneumocytes — Inflammatory cytokines impair surfactant synthesis and increase alveolar permeability, leading to non‑cardiogenic pulmonary oedema (ARDS).

*After this note, you should be able to differentiate cardiogenic from non-cardiogenic pulmonary oedema, understand their pathophysiology, recognise clinical features, interpret investigations, and initiate emergency management.
Normal PCWP (<18 mmHg) in the presence of bilateral infiltrates points towards non-cardiogenic pulmonary oedema (ARDS).
Fluid Overload: Exercise extreme caution with aggressive fluids in patients with severe malaria (risk of non-cardiogenic pulmonary oedema) and acute renal failure.
| Chest X-ray | Pulmonary oedema, pneumonia. | May show signs of non-cardiogenic pulmonary oedema in severe malaria. |
Non cardiogenic pulmonary oedema doesn’t usu respond to diuretic Tx, (CPAP) or (PEEP) ventilatory support may be reqd.
Diffuse alveolar damage → increased capillary permeability → protein-rich exudate floods alveoli (non-cardiogenic pulmonary oedema, distinguishing it from cardiogenic oedema)

qs.q: A recipient develops hypotension and respiratory distress presenting as non-cardiogenic pulmonary oedema within six hours of a blood transfusion. Which reaction has most likely occurred?
qs.e: TRALI is characterized by hypotension and respiratory distress caused by donor anti-leucocyte antibodies reacting against recipient white blood cells. TACO involves volume overload and presents with hypertension rather than hypotension.
